Gradsul — GM Notes

Days 12–15: after @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1FordJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1FdPgSetup00]{The Fallow Ford}, before @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GFeeJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GfPgSetup00]{The Grey Fee}. GM only — not for reading aloud, not for showing.

What this is

Colour, mostly. The @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1QRefJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1QrPgRun0000]{Run Sheet} gives Gradsul one line and one sentence that has to be said; this journal is the scene around that sentence. Three read-alouds, about seven minutes at the table in all: Into Gradsul (Day 12, about two and a half minutes), The Kestrel Wife (Day 12, about three, ending on the fire rule) and Out of the Sheldomar (Day 15, a little over a minute). And three pictures for the table.

The one thing that must happen

Roke's fire rule, said on his deck on Day 12. It is the last paragraph of The Kestrel Wife, in the same words as @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1BriefJrnl00.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1BrPgCal0000]{Party Calibration & the Fire Rule}. If you change one, change the other.

Master Roke and Caelith

@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-actors.Actor.BR2T1ActRoke0000]{Master Orin Roke} is Caelith's arrangement, made the way Caelith makes them: through an agent, in drafts, at a distance. A Yeomanry man paid Roke for passage and letters — five passengers, their bales, and whatever sealed post rides with them — and told him the story about wool. Roke has decided, deliberately, that the story is true (@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1NpcsJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1NpPgRoke000]{Roke's page}).

So he knows the mark on their letter: a quill above a closed gate, Caelith's seal. He has carried it east before. He will not break it, he will not say a name on a quay, and he will not ask them a single question; he expects the same courtesy back. Play him as a man who has been paid not to be curious and means to earn every copper of it. It is also, if anyone is looking, the first hint of how the Grey Fee finds them: he is a trader before he is anybody's courier.

On the quay, Vole matters more than Caelith does. A real Keoish drover vouching for them out loud is worth more than any letter they carry (@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1NpcsJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1NpPgVole000]{Vole's page}), and the read-aloud has him do it.

Variants

  • Vole's goodbye follows @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1FordJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1FdPgTally00]{The Visibility Tally}: Into Gradsul has one bracketed line per tier. Use the one the ford earned.
  • Sev. If the drover died at the ford, use the bracketed line for it. Nobody says his name.
  • Samples lost at the ford. The three days and the hundred and forty gold from @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1FordJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1FdPgTerr000]{Terrain, the Cart Clock & Outcomes} happen here, and cost the party no time: the Kestrel Wife does not sail until Day 15 anyway. Only the gold, and a factor who will remember selling wool to a wool delegation. Vole knows which factors are honest — let him send them to one.
  • If they will not leave, or try to hire their own hull, use the stall rails on the @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1QRefJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1QrPgRun0000]{Run Sheet}.

Showing the pictures

The last three pages of this journal carry nothing but a picture and a line of caption, so Show to Players exposes nothing: Gradsul — The Wool Quays as the carts come into the market, The Kestrel Wife — Going Aboard when Roke appears at the rail, and Out of the Sheldomar for Gianni at the prow on Day 15.

Per-PC beats

Marked in the read-aloud pages where they fire, outside the read-aloud text. Each goes to its player quietly, in a sentence or two, and is never explained afterward. Alicia reaches for her patron at the Foaming Tower. Kitty is invisible in Gradsul and noticed on the plank. Elle is offered a splicing lesson. Gianni goes to the prow. Selvara has the stair again on the first night out. See @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.pc-threads.JournalEntry.BR2PcThreadsJrnl]{Per-PC Plot Threads}.

Ashore at night

Days 12 to 14 are otherwise empty. The city is in @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GzetJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GzPgGM00000]{Gradsul — A Gazetteer} (map: @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-scenes.Scene.BR2T1ScnGrad0000]{Gradsul, City Map (GM)}), its people are in @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GPplJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1PpPgOffic00]{Gradsul — Who's Who}, and if the party goes looking for trouble it is waiting at the Mermaid's Inn: @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GullJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GuPgGM00000]{The Gull's Job}, an optional heist that costs no days. Wick is the easiest hook into it.

Wick Ferrin

@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GBckJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GbPgClock00]{The Grey-Back} asks you to name him days before he goes over the rail. This is where: he is the young hand who comes down the plank for their bales. Gradsul is his home port, and he has a wife up in the town. Let them like him.

Into Gradsul

Day 12, late afternoon. The Keoish cart road runs its last miles down the west bank of the Sheldomar to the sea, and Vole's carts are still with them. Show Gradsul — The Wool Quays as the carts come into the market.

Read aloud

You smell Gradsul an hour before you see it: river mud, tar and salt, and under all of it wet wool, because half the autumn clip of Keoland is coming down this road with you. The Sheldomar has been widening beside you for two days, brown and slow and busy — grain barges, rafts of Dreadwood timber, a long galley pulling upstream with her oars lifting all together like the legs of a beetle.

Then the road tops one last low rise, and the river stops being a river and becomes a harbour.

Gradsul lies along the water as far as you can see in either direction. Long ranks of flat-roofed warehouses stand at the waterline, their stone stained dark to a man's height by a hundred years of spray. Behind them the city climbs in tiers of slate and whitewash; in front of them the masts stand so thick along the quays that the harbour looks like a wood in winter. At the end of the outer mole, with the surf breaking white around its foot, there is a squat round tower of grey stone.

Vole points at it with his whip. “The Foaming Tower. Osprem's house. There's not a hand in this port will step aboard anything till he's rung that bell.”

Beat — Alicia, quietly. When Vole points at the tower, she reaches for her patron out of habit, the way every hand in this port reaches for Osprem. The same distant attentiveness as in Loftwick: alert, listening, and saying nothing.

The oxen know the way better than Vole does. The carts grind down through the warehouse quarter and out into the open market, where Gradsul is selling everything the Flanaess makes to everybody it sends. Suel-fair faces and Oeridian brown in the same crowd; a dozen accents, a dozen coinages; a woman with a tray of hot fish pies who has plainly seen stranger things than five armed westerners before breakfast. Nobody looks twice at you.

Beat — Kitty, quietly. Nobody looks twice at her either. Gradsul has seen tieflings; Gradsul has seen everything. It is the first time since Loftwick, and it will not last past the plank.

At the wool tents Vole climbs down and wrings each of your hands in turn, as though you were family he did not expect to see again. He tells you which factors in this city are honest, which wool-house will give five people a clean room, and how much to pay for it, and how much they will ask.

[If Sev lived:] Behind him, Sev says goodbye to Gianni in what he swears is her own accent.
[If Sev died at the ford:] Nobody says Sev's name. Vole holds Gianni's hand a moment longer than the others'.

[Quiet:] “I'll tell them the western buyers can handle themselves,” he says, “and that's all I'll tell them.”
[Mixed:] “And I'll tell them about that blade,” he says to Alicia, delighted, “because nobody in Gradsul is going to believe me.”
[Loud:] He has already started telling it. He is telling it to the man unloading the next cart over, with both hands, and the man has stopped unloading to listen.

Then he insists on walking you down to the water himself.

The Kestrel Wife

Day 12, the same afternoon. The hull and her master's name are in the party's papers: Caelith's arrangement (see the GM Notes page). Show The Kestrel Wife — Going Aboard when Roke appears at the rail. End on the fire rule.

Read aloud

The Kestrel Wife is not hard to find. You ask for her at three wharves, and three men point you down the same quay with the same expression — the expression of men who have pointed at her before. She lies at the far end: broad in the beam, high-sided, deep in the water, a tar-black hull with a faded ochre strake along it, and a smell of raw fleece that reaches you before her name does. A plank runs up from the quay to her waist, and a line of stevedores is walking bales up it two at a time.

Her master is at the rail. Short, wide, weathered to the colour of a saddle, in a good coat that has plainly come out of a chest for the occasion. He watches you the whole length of the quay and does not wave.

Vole does the waving for him. “Orin! Here's your westerners. I came down the whole road with them and they're sound, every one — I'll stand for them in any tent in this city.” Half the wharf hears him. It does more for your story than anything you are carrying.

[Whoever does the talking] hands up your letter. Roke turns it over once and stops at the wax — a quill above a closed gate — and looks at it about as long as it takes to read a name, though there is no name on it. Then he puts it inside his coat without breaking it.

“Roke. Master.” He doesn't offer a hand; there's a rope in it. “You're the wool delegation. You're paid for — you and your bales and your post — and that's an end of it. I've carried that mark east before. I don't open what I carry and I don't ask what I'm carrying, and on this hull that goes both ways. Come up, then.”

A young hand with tar to the elbows comes down the plank for your sample bales and takes two at once to show he can. Wick Ferrin, he says, Gradsul born, and does any of you know how to splice? He is delighted when none of you does.

Beat — Kitty, quietly. On the plank, one of the older hands steps out of her road and touches the iron of the rail as she passes. He does not look at her again. (GM: Mattick Sarn will, on Day 29.)

Beat — Elle, quietly. Wick's offer is meant for her; he has watched how she moves and decided she would pick it up fastest. If she says yes, he teaches her on Day 19. (GM: if the margin-note beat from her thread has not fired yet, any temple library in Gradsul will do — see @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.pc-threads.JournalEntry.BR2PcThreadsJrnl]{Per-PC Plot Threads}.)

Roke walks you aft. “She sails on the morning tide three days from now, when the last of the clip's aboard. You'll berth aft among the bales — it's dry, and you'll stop smelling it after a week. You'll eat with the crew, you'll keep out from under their feet, and when I tell you to go below, you'll go below and not ask me why.”

He looks at the five of you for a while, and then at the bales, and then back.

“No fire on my deck. Not for anything. Not if we're sinking, not if we're boarded, not if your own hair's alight — you come to me and I'll find you a bucket. I've seen a wool hull go up. It took four minutes and there was nothing left to bury.”

After the last line

Stop there. That is the sentence the second encounter is built on; whatever the table says next, let Roke answer it in as few words as he can find. If Vole's story had a fireball in it, Roke heard it on the wharf like everybody else, and his look on that last line rests on whoever threw it. The fire rule's consequences are on @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1BriefJrnl00.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1BrPgCal0000]{Party Calibration & the Fire Rule}.

Out of the Sheldomar

Day 15, the morning tide. Read as the Kestrel Wife clears the river mouth. If Gianni goes forward, show her Out of the Sheldomar with her beat.

Read aloud

The Kestrel Wife comes off the quay on the morning tide with a great deal of shouting and no hurry at all. Gradsul slides by — the warehouses, the tiers of whitewash, the market already loud — and then the Foaming Tower, close enough to hear its bell, and every hand aboard who isn't hauling on something touches his forehead to it as it passes.

Then the mouth of the Sheldomar opens, and there is nothing in front of you at all. Grey-green water to the edge of the world. A long low swell coming in under the bow. The coast behind you going soft, and then blue, and then gone.

Up in the bows, past the anchor cable and the last of the lashed bales, there is a place at the rail where the whole ship is behind you and nothing else is ahead. The spray comes over it now and then. None of the crew goes there unless they have to. It is the best seat on the hull.

Beat — Gianni, quietly. Show her Out of the Sheldomar. Every road she has walked lately has had somebody's hand on it. Out here there is nothing to recut, and nobody can scrape the sea off a chart. It is the first time in weeks she has let her shoulders down.

Beat — Selvara, quietly. The first night out, the stair comes back: the same torchlight, the same seventh step, the same mark she cannot focus on. Nothing new. The sea does not keep it away.

Kitty, and anyone else without sea legs, pays for the swell for three days (@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1BriefJrnl00.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1BrPgDays000]{The Six Weeks — Day Calendar}). The next thing that happens on this hull is Roke's first unannounced port, around Day 20.
